== Biography ==
=== Merchant family and corrected index review — 31 October 2026 ===
The 1935 printed Glasgow burgess register has been visually inspected. On 14 September 1795 John Glasgow, merchant, entered as husband of Helen, lawful daughter of James Smith, mason and burgess/guild brother (printed p.197, PDF 207). On 1 July 1817 Alexander Glasgow, merchant in Wilson’s Court, Argyle Street, entered as eldest son of John Glasgow, merchant and burgess/guild brother (p.306, PDF 316). On 3 May 1844 John Glasgow, merchant, entered as a younger son of John Glasgow, merchant and burgess/guild brother (p.450, PDF 460). The first entry strongly identifies the maintained John-1348/Helen Smith household; the sons are supported comparisons with Alexander-971 and John-1355. The sons’ entries do not name their mother, and the three admissions must not be treated as a literal statement that all three men form one family. These are inspected published register transcriptions; the underlying manuscript admission registers are unread.

Burke’s Visitation, vol.2, printed armorial section p.67 (PDF 341), has now been read in the scan. It explicitly describes Alexander of Old Court, formerly Auchinraith, as eldest son of the late John Glasgow and Helen, daughter of James Smith, and grandson of Alexander Glasgow, merchant, and Agnes Monro of Edinburgh. The family passage was already quoted in the held biography; inspecting it is not discovery of a previously unknown grandfather name. The underlying Lyon matriculation remains unread.

The FamilySearch citation X17D-67M was checked directly: John was born 13 October 1771 and christened 19 October 1771 at Barony, parents Alexander Glasgow and Mary Munro. The copied 3 December 1765 date attached to that same citation is wrong; no independent 1765 record was verified in this review. This corrects the source account, not the vital fields or later identity of either modern John profile.

The independently identified John–Helen Smith merchant household now has inspected burgess evidence, and Burke explicitly gives its Alexander grandfather with a Monro wife associated with Edinburgh. That rare paired family description is more specific than the earlier chronological comparison with Alexander-1309’s Alexander/Mary Munro household, whose 1757 marriage was recorded in Edinburgh and Barony. The corrected 1771 Barony child fits the merchant’s possible generation. This modestly strengthens the whole existing father-profile hypothesis from 38% to 45% Possible; it does not make it Probable. Burke names Agnes Monro, not the documented Mary Munro of Alexander-1309’s couple. Their identity cannot be assumed, and the 1771 child has no inspected occupation, wife or estate bridge identifying him as the merchant rather than the Colinton account John-1304. The merchant’s circa 1770 birth is an inherited estimate, not independent corroboration. Retain both modern Johns and the current father selection, all mothers, vital fields and upstream grades. No new father attachment or merge follows. The 1741 childhood identification of Alexander-1309 is not certified by this review. Exact percentages are subjective judgements, not measured probabilities.<ref>[https://www.electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso51scotuoft.pdf Glasgow Burgesses and Guild Brethren 1751–1846 (1935)], pp.197,306,450 (PDF 207,316,460); [https://archive.org/details/visitationofseat185402burk/page/n340/mode/1up Burke, Visitation, vol.2, armorial p.67 (PDF 341)]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X17D-67M FamilySearch X17D-67M], inspected 31 October 2026. Printed sources and derivative index read; manuscript admission, parish and Lyon originals unread.</ref>

Alexander Glasgow was christened on 9 March 1741 in the parish of Kirknewton, Midlothian, Scotland. He was the son of [[Glasgow-3052|Andrew Glasgow]] and [[Clerk-313|Janet Clerk]].<ref name="Birth1741">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-P56 : 12 February 2020), Alexander Glasgow, 1741.</ref>

He married '''[[Munro-4088|Mary Munro]]''' (recorded as Munrow) in July/August 1757. Their marriage was recorded in both Edinburgh, Midlothian, and Barony, Lanarkshire, a common practice when the bride and groom resided in different parishes.<ref name="Marriage1757">"Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYMW-HXK), Alexander Glasgow and Mary Monro, 31 Jul 1757, Edinburgh, Midlothian; AND "Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYWC-Q5G), Alexander Glasgow and Mary Munrow, 4.co.uk/transcript?id=GBOR%2FGLA%2FRAMSHORN%2FBUR%2F000490), burial of Mary Glasgow on 22 January 1779, daughter of Alexr. Glasgow, glasgow regt., age 6m. Ref: 644/1/59.</ref>

Alexander and Mary had the following children:
* [[Glasgow-1348|John Glasgow]].{{Citation Needed}}
* [[Glasgow-1304|John Glasgow]], christened 3 December 1765 in Glasgow, Lanarkshire.<ref name="John1765">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X17D-67M), John Glasgow, 1765; citing Glasgow, Lanarkshire, Scotland, reference - 2:17L1JNP.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-3300|Barbara (Glasgow) Carswell]].{{Citation Needed}}
* [[Glasgow-3121|Mary Glasgow]], who died of smallpox at 6 months old and was buried on 22 January 1779 in the Ramshorn parish of Glasgow.

The date and place of his death are unknown.

== Research Notes ==
=== Father confidence review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-3052]] is assessed at 89% (probable). The held biography cites the9March1741 Kirknewton/East Calder Alexander as son of Andrew Glasgow and Janet Clerk. The selected Andrew account is the maintained father in that parish and its estimated1720 generation is compatible. The full named couple and exact child event strongly identify the recorded family. However Andrew’s sparse profile lacks independent adult identification, and Alexander’s later Edinburgh/Glasgow identity is not connected by the baptism alone.

Probable89% for the selected profile pair, based on a retained citation rather than a newly inspected transcript/original. The proposed Andrew birth and his own father are not validated.

Next useful test: Verify the original1741 parent entry and Andrew/Janet household before pursuing Andrew’s uncertain James father.

Source basis already held: [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-P56 "Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-P56 : 12 February 2020), Alexander Glasgow, 1741.]. No new original was inspected in this review. This is an assessment of an existing attachment, not a new father.


'''Marriage Registrations in Two Parishes'''

Two marriage records exist for this couple with dates just a few days apart: one in Edinburgh and one in the Barony parish of Glasgow. This is not evidence of two different couples. It was standard practice in 18th-century Scotland for a couple's marriage banns to be proclaimed and recorded in both the bride's and the groom's home parishes if they lived separately before the wedding.

Given that Alexander was from Kirknewton (near Edinburgh) and the family subsequently lived and raised their children in Glasgow, it is almost certain that these two records refer to the same couple. One record represents his parish (Edinburgh) and the other represents hers (Barony, Glasgow).

=== Possible A. Glascow, 1794 arrival ===
A. Glascow from Glasgow is named with H. Jurriens from Riga and J. Mark from Königsbergen in a shipping-arrival report for 24 June 1794, under the Rotterdam dateline of 25 June.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1335425007/ Rotterdamse courant, 26 June 1794, p.2].</ref>

Only the initial A. is given. The list probably names a shipmaster, but it does not state a vessel, full forename, sex, family or personal origin. Glasgow is the departure port. P. L. Markwaarden in the following entry is a different person.

This may concern [[Glasgow-1309]]. Chronologically adult in 1794; occupation field says clerk, with no maritime source or Rotterdam connection.
